capabilities.description: The Trades ledger's session acts that remove nothing. A session is one journal file under the trades folder, named `<symbol folder>/<file>.csv` for simulator history or `broker/<symbol folder>/<file>.csv` for the sibling real-trades folder; three replays of one tape are three sessions. `list` returns the sessions holding a trade the ledger's filter keeps (source pills, a civil date span, and a search where `#tag` tokens must all be on the trade and other words must appear in the session's name or default label), newest first and bounded, and changes nothing. `rename` and `tag` append a line to the session's own file (the last line wins, the trade columns never change), the live session included. `view` sets the active tab's ledger filter and folds sessions shut or open, and answers what the ledger then shows; with no field it only reads. Deleting a session is `session.journal.delete`. Open an exact session or origin-specific civil-day report with `session.report.open`. Source filters broker and simulator separate execution origins; real retains its legacy meaning of simulator-on-live-feed, replay selects simulator replays, and both includes all origins. Refusals carry `details.code`: invalid_session, session_not_found, trade_not_found, invalid_tag, session_unreadable, writes_refused, write_failed, no_ledger. Every edit and view change journals `session.journal.changed`, and every open ledger and report re-reads the folder after an edit.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Every action names its session by file. A repeated rename, tag or view writes the same name, tags or view again and leaves the same state; a stale listing can only name a session that has since moved, which the next edit refuses.
capabilities.title: List, name or tag trade journal sessions, or set the Trades ledger's view

A `primary` outside the three modes is refused with control.invalid_request and changes nothing. A set that moves the choice journals `session.pnl_display.changed`; repeating it changes nothing and answers `changed: false`.

capabilities.description: Open the same performance report as the Trades session context menu. action=session selects only that session; action=day requires YYYY-MM-DD in the display timezone and selects every instrument and session of that origin on the clicked day. The session must hold a trade on that day. action=whole_day takes origin (simulator or broker) and day instead of a session and selects every trade of that origin closed that day, as the day header's context menu does. action=tag takes origin and a tag (with or without #, case ignored) and selects every trade of that origin carrying it over all history, as a trade's Report #tag menu does. Simulator and broker are never summed. action=ordinary restores the ordinary Sim live report for the chart symbol over all time; pass no session or day. action=sources with sources sets their union, exits session/day context scope and preserves visible symbol/date filters: broker, real (Sim live including legacy), replay, simulator (real + replay), both (all). An empty array selects none. Omitting sources reads the current report without opening it or emitting session.report.opened. action=inspect also reads without opening or emitting. action=days sets the picked days outright, as the report's Dates popover does: days is a list of up to 92 distinct YYYY-MM-DD civil days in the display timezone, any order, contiguous or not; a trade is in when the day it closed on is listed. Repeating the call sets the same days; an empty list clears them. A day that is not a real YYYY-MM-DD date refuses the whole call. action=symbols sets the symbols the report reads outright, as its multi-select does (empty reads every symbol); a symbol with no journal folder refuses with unknown_symbol. action=merge with a currency merges every curve into one money curve in it: each trade converted at the stored rate of the civil day it closed on, USDT and USDC read as USD, a pair converting both ways; trades with no point value or no rate that day are left out and listed in merged.unconverted, never guessed. The currency must be one listed in currencies (the selection's currencies plus USD), else invalid_currency; it becomes the default Merge all reads in. currency null reads per asset. Points never merge across instruments: a points report keeps one curve per instrument and says so in merge_note. These actions return symbols, currencies, merge and merged (currency, assets, rates per day, unconverted, net, caption). action=clear_dates clears the picked days, restoring the selected period. action=period sets Today, 7d, 30d, 90d, All or a custom duration such as 12h anchored to the newest close, and clears picked days. Date and period edits retain symbol, sources and tag restrictions; picked days other than a day context's own day take a whole-session or day context out of force and keep its origin. These actions return applied_days (oldest first; past 92 days, only the newest 92), applied_day_count and timezone. Refusals carry details.code invalid_dates or invalid_period. Returns normalized sources, window, context, open/loaded status, trade count and net points. Retries set the same selection, never toggle. Session keys are <symbol>/<file>.csv for the simulator and broker/<symbol>/<file>.csv for real-trades, independent of custom names. Session, day and ordinary actions replace prior symbol, period, source and session filters. Returns the opened scope, trade count, net points and counts of unreadable files and skipped rows in the scanned history; events.read reconciles a lost open response through session.report.opened. Refusals: invalid_currency, unknown_symbol, invalid_session, session_not_found, session_unreadable, day_not_in_session, invalid_tag, no_trades_in_scope, no_ledger. Never places orders or writes history.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Repeating a request opens the same scope from current history; deleted sessions are refused before changing the report.
capabilities.title: Open or filter a performance report

capabilities.title: Cancel a working order

capabilities.description: Places one market, limit or stop order on the charted symbol, optionally with the protective stop and target that arm when it fills. The kind is stated, never inferred from where the market happens to be - a kind that cannot rest at the given price is refused with the reason, in the venue's own words.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Every price is judged against the market at the moment the order lands, not at the moment it was written: a limit that would fill at once, or a stop that would trigger at once, is refused with the reason. A caller working from a stale chart can therefore place an order at a level that has gone stale, but never one the venue would not have accepted from a caller reading the live tape.
capabilities.title: Place a simulated order

capabilities.description: Exits the open position at the next print and removes every working order, in one call, so the account is never half-flat between two calls. Risk-reducing: it only ever takes exposure off. Flat with nothing working, it changes nothing.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Names no order and no size: it flattens whatever the account holds when it lands, so a caller working from a stale read still ends flat.
capabilities.title: Go flat: close the position and cancel every working order

capabilities.description: Flips the open position in one market order for twice its size, protected by the ticket's offsets for the new side. The opening leg is measured by the risk per trade like any entry and refused with its sentence. Refused while flat: there is nothing to reverse.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: The size is the account's at the moment the call lands, never a size the caller read earlier. Not safe to retry: a second reversal flips the position back.
capabilities.title: Reverse the simulated position

capabilities.description: Says what one trade may lose - a fixed amount, or a share of the capital declared for the instrument's currency - and whether an entry whose stop risks more than that is refused. Shapes the size the next order would carry; changes no order that exists and never touches an open position.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: The call answers with the risk that is now set and with what it makes of the entry the ticket is holding, including the reason when it can name no size, so a caller sees the same sentence the trader is reading. It changes nothing that is already working.
capabilities.title: Set the risk per trade

capabilities.description: Walks the projected stop and target out from an aimed entry, the same distance on both sides, in ticks of the instrument. Zero puts the ruler away. Shapes what the next order would carry rather than changing one that exists - the read a trader takes before committing.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: The call answers with where the ruler actually landed, clamped to what the wheel itself can reach, so a caller that asked for more can see what it got. It changes nothing that is already working.
capabilities.title: Set the aim's ruler distance

capabilities.description: Sets which named exit strategy the next order rests with, or none for a bare order. Changes no order that already exists and never touches an open position; the same call the ticket's own selector makes.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: The call names the strategy it selected and answers with the one that is now set, so a caller working from a stale read can see that it chose something else. It changes nothing that is already working.
capabilities.title: Choose the ticket's exit ladder

capabilities.description: Closes one widget pane's floating window, as its close button does.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Closing a closed pane is the same state, so a stale or repeated call can only hide it.
capabilities.title: Close a widget pane

capabilities.description: Opens one widget pane in its floating window over the chart, reading the active tab: depth (the DOM ladder), big_trades, liquidations or open_interest. A pane whose data the feed does not provide opens and says so; provided reports which. Read what it paints with widget.read.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Opening an open pane is the same state, so a stale or repeated call can only show it.
capabilities.title: Open a widget pane

capabilities.description: Returns what one widget pane paints for the active tab, open or not: its chips, the rows it lays out, the empty-state sentence when it has no data, and every text item in paint order (at most 512). Built from the same scene the window draws, so the read and the screen agree.
capabilities.title: Read a widget pane

capabilities.description: On, every layout edit on a tab is written into its workspace a second after it stops, and the clean tabs on that workspace follow; a tab reads as modified only while its copy is not in its workspace: a write that failed (retried each quiet second until another tab saves that workspace), a second tab on that workspace holding edits (one copy is written: of every tab there holding edits, the active tab's, else the lowest id's), or a copy a restart brought back differing. Such a tab holds its edits as with autosave off: autosave never writes it, and closing it, switching it or exiting asks. Off, a tab holds its edits, marked, until workspace.save_to, and closing it asks. Turning it on saves every tab holding edits at once, one per workspace (never one marked as above), and answers each save; when one fails the setting stays on, the setting and the saves that landed are journaled, and the call refuses with workspace.write_failed whose details name auto_save and the workspaces saved. The desk keeps the choice; the workspace snapshot reads it as auto_save. This choice controls workspace configuration only; drawing writes are controlled independently by chart.drawings.autosave.set.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: The call names the state it wants, so a repeat answers changed false and writes only a save still owed, as after a failure.
capabilities.title: Turn auto save layout changes on or off

capabilities.description: Reads the palette the workspace menu's header swatch opens, for one workspace (left out, the active tab's): the sixteen presets with their index, name and Light and Dark values, which is current, which another workspace holds with its initials (a pick asks to swap), the last custom colour applied (the seventeenth swatch) and the colour a new workspace would take next. Set a colour with workspace.colour.set or drive the popover with workspace.colour.popover.
capabilities.title: Read a workspace's colour palette

capabilities.description: Acts on the palette popover under the workspace menu's header swatch, for the tab on screen, as a hand does: open (the menu too), close (the menu stays), pick a swatch (a free colour applies at once and closes the popover; one another workspace holds puts the swap question in the grid's place), custom (opens the Custom picker on a hex, #RRGGBB or RRGGBB, and answers its warnings: close to another workspace's colour, near the buy green or sell red, low contrast on a tab strip; none blocks), apply (Custom's colour, through the same path; a malformed hex answers hex_hint and changes nothing; an identical colour asks to swap) and answer (swap true takes the colour and gives the holder this workspace's old one, false cancels). Each answer is the popover's state. Any act but open while it is closed is refused with workspace.colour_popover_closed.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Opening twice leaves it open; a pick names its colour, so a repeat answers no change; an answer with the question gone is refused as closed or changes nothing.
capabilities.title: Drive the workspace colour popover

capabilities.description: Gives a workspace a colour: one of the sixteen presets by name (cobalt, orchid, sky, violet, slate, fuchsia, petrol, lavender, ultramarine, mauve, denim, grape, ink, plum, ice, blossom) or a custom #RRGGBB. The open tab paints its symbol in it, the capsule its tint, border and left bar, and the workspace menu its row's and header's slot. No two workspaces hold identical colours (the same value in either theme): a colour another workspace holds is refused with workspace.colour_taken, its details listing the holders in owners and, for a single holder, the colour it would get in owner_would_get. With swap true a single holder takes this workspace's old colour, named in swapped_with and holder_colour; two or more holders, or a swap that would give the holder a colour a third workspace matches, are refused even with swap. A new workspace takes the next free colour and a deleted one frees its own. Read the colours with workspace.list or on each tab of workspace.summary. The answer's warnings list what the colour warns, none of which blocks: kind close (hard to tell from the named workspace's colour), near_buy, near_sell, or low_contrast (lost on the named theme's tab strip, dark or light). An applied custom colour becomes the palette's last custom colour (workspace.colour.palette). A name no workspace has is refused with workspace.unknown, a colour that is neither a preset nor #RRGGBB with workspace.colour_invalid.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Default is protected against direct changes and swaps. The call names the colour it wants, so a repeat answers changed false and writes nothing.
capabilities.title: Give a workspace a colour

capabilities.description: Deletes a workspace and moves the tabs on it to Default. A tab with unsaved edits keeps them, marked Default •. Default cannot be deleted. For 10 seconds, until the answer's undo_until_unix_ms, workspace.delete.undo brings it back with its recipe, colour and tabs, as Manage workspaces' Undo does.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: A repeat finds no such workspace and is refused with workspace.unknown; nothing is written.
capabilities.title: Delete a workspace

capabilities.description: Takes back a workspace.delete within 10 seconds of it (its answer's undo_until_unix_ms), as Manage workspaces' Undo and Ctrl+Z do: the workspace comes back with its recipe and colour, and the tabs the delete moved that are still open and still on Default move back. When its colour was taken meanwhile it takes the next free one, named in colour with recoloured true. Refused with workspace.undo_expired after the 10 seconds, workspace.unknown with no recent delete of that name, and workspace.name_taken when a workspace took the name meanwhile.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: A repeat after the Undo landed answers changed false and writes nothing.
capabilities.title: Undo a workspace delete

capabilities.description: Opens save_as, new or manage for a tab, defaulting to the active tab. New previews timeframe_ms, charts (1-8) and custom_hex in one form. A blank name uses Workspace N. Invalid or occupied colours stay visible and block Create. Manage shows the locked Default first. Opening or cancelling writes nothing. An unknown tab is refused with workspace.unknown_tab.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Opening a dialog twice leaves one open, the create dialogs reset to their suggested name and colour.
capabilities.title: Open a workspace dialog

capabilities.description: Lists every saved workspace with a one-line summary (panes, intervals, indicator count), its colour and the open tabs using it, The immutable factory Default comes first. Which workspace a tab uses and whether it holds edits is also on each tab in workspace.summary.
capabilities.title: List the workspaces

capabilities.description: Creates a clean workspace with charts (1-8, default 1) and timeframe_ms (current time interval, otherwise 5m), on a generic Layout N. All charts use the chosen interval. Existing workspace edits are parked and restored when revisiting it; dropped_edits is false. Other tabs and market-owned drawings are preserved. An omitted or blank name requires an idempotency key and chooses Workspace N. An explicit name must be unique. Colour is a preset or #RRGGBB; omitted selects the next free color, and a held color is refused without swapping. Invalid choices are refused before mutation. The New workspace form's Create action; open and preview it with workspace.dialog.open.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Repeat the same payload and key to replay the original result. An explicit name also permits an unkeyed request; repeating it refuses with workspace.name_taken.
capabilities.title: Make a new, empty workspace for a tab

capabilities.description: Renames a workspace; the tabs on it follow. Default cannot be renamed, and an empty or taken name is refused with the reason.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: Naming the name it already has writes nothing and answers changed false.
capabilities.title: Rename a workspace

capabilities.description: Puts the tab back on its workspace as saved: pane sizes, each chart's bar rule, chart type, indicators and layers; a bar rule the workspace does not name goes back to the one the tab opened with. Drawings, orders and other tabs are not touched, and nothing is written. The dropped edits are held for workspace.revert.undo until the workspace is saved or the tab switches workspace; each revert replaces the last. A tab without unsaved edits answers changed false.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: A repeat finds no edits and answers changed false; the held edits stay.
capabilities.title: Discard a tab's unsaved layout edits

capabilities.description: Puts back the unsaved edits the tab's last workspace.revert dropped, unsaved again. Answers changed false when there are none: nothing reverted, the workspace saved or the tab switched since, or the tab holds edits of its own since, which a revert drops first.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: The held edits are taken once: a repeat answers changed false.
capabilities.title: Bring back the edits a revert dropped

capabilities.description: Makes a workspace of what the tab shows and puts the tab on it, in colour (a preset's name or #RRGGBB; left out, the next free colour). No other tab changes. An empty or taken name is refused with the reason; a colour another workspace holds is refused with workspace.colour_taken, never swapped on create; one that is neither with workspace.colour_invalid. The Save as new workspace dialog's Save; open it with workspace.dialog.open. Layout configuration is committed independently of drawings; paused drawings remain paused.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: A repeat from the tab that made the name writes nothing and answers changed false.
capabilities.title: Save a tab as a new workspace

capabilities.description: Writes the tab's edits into the workspace it uses and answers the other tabs that changed: the ones on that workspace without edits of their own. A tab with edits keeps them. Default refuses overwrite. Use workspace.save_as to keep its edits. Save also commits layout configuration (selection, count, names, pane geometry and timeframes). Drawing autosave and its saved snapshot are independent; Save never writes paused drawings.
capabilities.stale_input_safety: A repeat finds no edits, writes nothing and answers changed false.
capabilities.title: Save a tab's edits to its workspace

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports each pane's drawings with tool, band, scope, lock and visibility state, and the author of anything the trader did not place by hand.

AnnotationBand.description:
Which value axis of the pane an annotation's anchor prices are read on.
Omitted: the candles' price axis, so every call written before indicator
bands existed means what it always meant.

oneOf.description: The candles' price axis.

One indicator pane's own value axis, named by the `kind` and `ordinal`
the pane's indicators snapshot reports (`native.cvd`, `0`). Anchor
`price` is then that indicator's value: a CVD level, not a price.

client_name.description: The client's own name, as it introduced itself at the handshake.

DrawingOriginSnapshot.description: Where a migration merged a drawing from. See [`DrawingSnapshot::origin`].

all_windows.description:
Whether every chart of the same market and workspace shows it,
whatever layout it shows ("All windows"). Legacy unscoped entries
retain their prior flag. Written only when true for compatibility with
v1 readers.

annotation_band.description:
The same band in the shape an `annotate.*.create` call takes as
`band`, so a listed mark's band can be handed straight back; absent for
a time-only mark, which has no value axis. Optional in the schema only
so v1 readers stay compatible.

author.description:
Set when something other than the trader's hand placed this object.
Absent is the trader's own. An object an agent placed must never be
indistinguishable from one the trader placed.

band.description: The value axis the anchors were placed against.

drawing_id.description:
Identity, stable while the object lives. Position in the list is not
identity: removing an earlier object renumbers positions and never
this.

follows_ground.description:
Its look is the tool's factory look, worn in the factory ink of the
ground of the pane it sits on and repainted when the theme or the
pane's background changes; a saved default never reaches it. False
when it opened from a saved default, once its look is the trader's own
(any edit of colour, width, fill or a tool's look), and for a mark
saved before marks recorded it. Optional in the schema only so v1
readers stay compatible.

foreign_market.description:
The tab changed the instrument under this mark. Time survives a symbol
switch and price does not, so the anchors still resolve while the level
means nothing on the chart it is now over. The object stays and says
so, rather than pretending to be a level on this market.

hidden.description:
This object's own eye. It is not the whole answer to "is it on screen":
the pane's `layer_hidden` above hides every object regardless.

layout_id.description:
The strip layout it belongs to, the `layout_id` the layout-tab calls
name; absent for one saved before drawings recorded their layout.

magnet.description:
This object's own OHLC magnet (`annotate.drawing_magnet.set`), which
snaps its drags whatever the rail's `magnet` above says; always false
for a tool that snaps by its own rule. Optional in the schema only so
v1 readers stay compatible.

off_series.description:
This pane's series does not reach the market instant an anchor was
placed at — the mark survived a re-cut, a rewind or a symbol switch,
but no longer sits on the data it was drawn against.

origin.description:
The layout and contract a migration merged this object from, when one
did. A merged market is labelled, never passed off as one history.
Optional in the schema only so v1 readers stay compatible.

scope.description:
`all_charts` when every chart of its market, workspace and named
layout shows it at any timeframe; `this_chart` pins it to its bars.

time_projected.description:
An anchor's market time is projected past the newest bar of a tick,
volume or renko chart from the recent bars' pace, not read off a bar:
an estimate, which the inspector labels. Written only when true.

user_label_present.description:
True when the trader gave the object their own name. The name itself is
their words and is never published.

layer_hidden.description:
The toolrail's "Hide all" is on, so nothing below is drawn whatever its
own eye says. A separate switch from the per-object `hidden` — "show
all" restores exactly the per-object visibility it found — and stated
here rather than folded into each row, so an agent that turns the layer
back on knows which marks it will get.

selected_index.description:
Position of the selected drawing within this pane's own list — which is
`drawing_count` long and not the possibly truncated `drawings` page
above. Present only when the selection is on this pane.

magnet.description:
The drawing rail's OHLC magnet (`annotate.magnet.set`), present
whether or not the rail is on screen. Always written; optional in
the schema only so v1 readers stay compatible.

snapshot_scopes.title: Drawings

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports each pane's indicators with their declared plots, effective inputs, latest readings and pending failures.

IndicatorFailureSnapshot.description:
Why an indicator is not answering. The stable `detail` is a code a client
branches on; the underlying message is withheld whenever the trader's own
script wrote it.

bar_index.description: The bar the evaluation failed on, when the failure names one.

state.description:
`error` — disabled until rebuilt — or `stale`: a hot reload failed and
the previously running version is still evaluating.

user_text_redacted.description: True when a message exists but is the trader's own text.

name.description: Stable identifier — the persistence key and the script argument name.

options.description: The fixed choices, when the input declares any.

text_present.description:
True when this is a `string` input the script left unconstrained, and a
value is bound. Free text is the trader's own words, so the value is
withheld and only its presence reported; a `string` input constrained
to a fixed option set is an enumeration, not prose, and its value is
published above.

value.description:
The bound value, rendered in the input's own vocabulary. Absent for a
free-text input: see `text_present`.

committed_bar_count.description:
Committed bars this indicator has evaluated. Tracked rather than
derived from the plot columns: an indicator whose whole output is
candle paint declares no plots at all.

failure.description:
Why this indicator is not answering, when it is not. Absent means it
evaluated cleanly.

hidden.description:
The eye toggle. A hidden indicator keeps evaluating, so its readings
below are still current.

inputs.description:
Every declared input paired with the value currently bound to it —
what the settings dialog would open with.

kind.description:
The constructor it was added through (`native.cvd`, `script.zigzag`),
durable across remove and re-add in a way the slot is not.

mouse_vertical_line.description: Whether price-chart hover is mirrored into this non-price pane.

ordinal.description:
Which instance of that kind this is, assigned once at birth. Two EMAs
on one pane are told apart by this, never by position.

overlay.description: True = drawn over the price chart; false = its own sub-pane below it.

preview_present.description: Whether a forming-bar preview frame exists right now.

slot_id.description:
The slot the running instance answers to. Reused after a remove, so it
addresses an instance *now* and is not an identity across a session.

source_kind.description:
`native` or `script` — whether we wrote it or the trader did. It
decides whether any diagnostic text is theirs, and so redacted.

latest_value.description:
The most recent committed value of this column. Absent when the column
has no rows yet, or when the value is not finite — a gap in a series is
a gap, never a zero.

offset_bars.description: Horizontal shift in bars; positive is rightward.

plot_index.description: Index of the column this spec describes, in declaration order.

renders_as_marker.description: True when the column renders as markers instead of through its style.

snapshot_scopes.title: Indicators

snapshot_scopes.description: Bounded active TOML, paint revision, source and last-known persistence status; no filesystem paths.

choice.description: dark, light, or custom; exact bundled source identity, never RGB matching.

durable.description: Last successful load/save. Files are not polled for external edits.

load_failed.description: Startup fell back to Dark after an invalid/unreadable selected file.

origin.description: bundled_dark, session, or selected_store; never a local path.

revision.description: Paint revision: semantic equality does not invalidate rendering caches.

source.description: The active candidate's original TOML, including omitted Dark fallbacks.

snapshot_scopes.title: Appearance state

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports every pane's bar rule, revisions, viewport, price range, and coverage.

BarProgressSnapshot.description: The forming bar's progress in its rule's own unit.

done.description:
What has accumulated: the count, the milliseconds a time bar has run,
or an imbalance rule's signed running total.

target.description:
Where the bar closes; absent for an imbalance rule, which has no
fixed target.

unit.description:
The unit both figures count in: `ms` for a time rule, else the rule's
own (`ticks`, a volume or notional unit, an imbalance measure).

venue_candles.description:
The venue candles the pane's prefix is built from, and whether more
are on their way; absent for a pane that reads none.

bar_progress.description:
How far the forming bar is from closing, as the last-price tag prints
it: a time rule's on the tab's market clock (the replay's playhead
while replaying). Absent with no forming bar to read. Optional on the
wire, as `uncounted_prints` is.

held_prints.description:
Prints the pane's rule holds uncut until they show it its price step
— a Renko pane's before its first brick. They form the in-progress
bar. Zero for every rule that reads no step. Optional on the wire, as
`uncounted_prints` is.

inferred_price_step.description:
The price step the pane's rule read off the pane's own prints and
cuts on — a Renko pane's, once its prints have shown it. Inferred,
never declared by a venue. Absent for a rule that reads no step, and
for one still reading it: `held_prints` says how many it holds.

off_grid_prints.description:
Prints off the price step the pane's rule froze: cut on that step and
counted, never snapped onto it. Zero for every rule that freezes none.

pane_index.description:
The pane's address within its tab — `0` the flow pane, `1..` the
context stack top to bottom — the number `layout.focus` takes.

price_tag_progress.description:
Whether the last-price tag prints that progress: the setting of the
pane's market (`chart.price_tag.progress.set`). Optional on the wire.

uncounted_prints.description:
Prints the pane's rule could place in no bar — a deal bar's prints
before its first counter reading. Zero for every other rule. The
number the chart-corner chip shows, as data.
Optional on the wire so v1 readers remain compatible with snapshots
produced before deal bars existed.

LaneWindowSnapshot.description:
How wide the live lane's window is, said the way the setting says it. An
`auto` window follows the recent bars' typical duration, so publishing one
resolved number would report a measurement as a setting.

fixed_ms.description: Present for `fixed`: the exchange milliseconds shown in the band.

zoom.description: Present for `auto`: `1.0` fits about one bar's worth of market time.

TapeViewSnapshot.description: The tape's time frame as a pane reports it.

end_unix_ms.description:
The past instant the right edge is held at; absent while it follows
live, where the edge is the moving tape clock.

follows_live.description: The right edge is now. False while the tape is held in the past.

retained_from_unix_ms.description:
First instant the retained tape is complete from: a past end cannot
hold the window further back than half of it before this.

window_ms.description: The market time the tape shows now, resolved.

VenueCandleState.description: Where asking the venue for older candles stands.

oneOf.description: Nothing out; scrolling near the oldest bar asks for more.
A request is out.
The venue's record starts at the oldest candle held.

VenueCandleStatus.description: The venue candles one pane reads.

interval_ms.description:
The interval the candles were asked for at: the pane's own, or the
coarser one folded into it.

last_reply_short.description:
Whether the last answer was cut short (a failed or throttled fetch):
the candles held are real, and more are asked for after a backoff.

tape.description: The native tape's own time frame; absent without a native tape.

visible_start_slot.description:
The slots the viewport asks the renderer to paint: generous by one bar
at each edge, so a bar partly off screen is drawn rather than clipped.
This is the pane's own notion of "visible", not the exact pixel set.

snapshot_scopes.title: Chart summary

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports the selected and active markets, source health, capabilities, and provenance.

ConnectionSnapshot.description:
The tab's `ConnectionState`. Carries words of its own, never the venue's:
like [`FeedNoticeSnapshot`] it publishes no provider text.

current_job.description: The job the header's slot is naming, in the words it uses.

last_connected_unix_ms.description: When the transport was last seen connected.

link.description:
`live`, `attempting`, `offline`, `quiet` or `no_transport`. `offline`
latches until data arrives, `feed.reconnect` is called or the transport
has stayed up for ten seconds.

overlay_up.description: The overlay stands over the panes with no bars.

reconnect_offered.description:
A `feed.reconnect` press is on offer on screen: the overlay's or the
status bar's.

status_word.description: The word the status bar shows, absent while a new session settles.

DealRecordingSnapshot.description: The recorder as the chrome reads it, on the wire.

counter_stale.description:
The counter has not moved for the stale span while prints kept
coming — REC on (state `stale`) or off, where the chart's chip says
`counter stale` or `counter stuck at 0` (`session_deals` 0).

deal_count_available.description: Whether a `trades` pane has a count to cut on right now.

error.description: The last write or read error, if the recorder hit one.

file.description: The file being written, while recording.

first_reading_unix_ms.description: When the first reading of this run arrived, written to a file or not.

loaded_days.description: Days whose readings were loaded into the panes this session.

record_by_default.description:
The standing choice: record by default wherever a feed carries a
counter — what the Tools menu's checkbox reads, saved with the
workspace.

recorded_days.description: Days recorded under this symbol, oldest first.

samples_written.description: Lines written to that file this run.

session_deals.description: The newest reading of the venue's session deal counter.

since_unix_ms.description:
Where the open file starts, on the tape's clock — the recording's own
"since", resumed or written this run. What the REC button shows.

state.description:
`off`, `recording`, `stale` (the tape flows, the counter does not),
`recorded` (the readings on screen came from a file) or `unsupported`
(the feed declares no counter; a day recorded earlier may still be
listed and loaded).

FeedBackfillSnapshot.description: A feed's refill of a reconnect hole: what it asked for and how it ended.

remaining_gap.description:
The part no print covers, on a `partial` refill; it is also one of
`tape_gaps`.

requested_from_unix_ms.description: The last print the chart held before the source went away.

requested_to_unix_ms.description: The oldest print the new session opened with.

trades_received.description: Prints received toward the refill, before the seams were deduplicated.

deal_counter.description: Defaults off for snapshots produced before deal counters existed.

history_boundary.description:
Why `history_paging` is off when the feed knows: `venue_retention`
means the venue keeps nothing older. Absent while paging is on, and
on a provider that never pages; optional, so additive to v1.

liquidations.description:
The derivative streams the widget panes 3 and 4 gate on; false on
every provider today. Optional, so additive to v1.

FeedGapSnapshot.description: A hole in the tape, in market time.

from_unix_ms.description: The last print before the silence.

roll_refused.description:
Why the configured roll off `unlisted_symbol` cannot run right now, as
the popup and the status word's hover say it. A restored tab rolls by
itself once the reason clears.

roll_to.description:
The contract the notice's Roll moves the tab to: the popup's first
control, and the one beside the status word and on an empty chart.
Absent when no roll is on offer.

rolled_from.description:
The contract the tab rolled off because the venue no longer lists it,
onto `active_symbol`: the note the status bar shows beside the status
word. Not a notice: it stands beside whatever `kind` says, through the
new feed's progress, connect and any trouble, until the tab's next
switch, reconnect or reload. Absent otherwise; additive to v1.

unlisted_symbol.description:
The contract the venue reported it does not list, from the feed's
structured report — not from the redacted words. When it is the tab's
`active_symbol`, `feed.contract.roll` from it is the popup's Roll
button: same rule, same refusals, and the `from_symbol` it takes.
Absent otherwise; an optional field is an additive change to the v1
payload.

contract_rolls.description: Which contract follows which on this feed, for feed.contract.roll.

FeedStallSnapshot.description:
A feed the chart has decided is stalled.

Carries no free text, for the same reason [`FeedNoticeSnapshot`] carries
none: the words name the venue and the terminal behind it, and the observe
tier does not publish them. What it does carry is the part a client can act
on — which of the two recovery capabilities the application is offering
first, and how long the feed has been like this.

needs_attention.description:
Whether this is unambiguously wrong (a transport that never landed or
dropped) or merely observed silence, which is also what a closed market
looks like. The interface colours the two differently and so should a
client deciding whether to say anything to the trader.

primary_recovery.description:
`reconnect` or `reload` — the capability that addresses this stall.
The other one is always available too.

text_availability.description: Why the words are not in this payload.

connection.description:
What every surface on screen says about this feed, from the one state
they all read. Optional, so additive to v1; the application always
reports it.

deal_recording.description:
The deal recorder, where the feed carries a deal counter; absent on
a feed without one. The same view the REC control draws.

feed_generation.description:
How many feed sessions this tab has taken over since it opened. It
advances by one on every respawn — a reconnect, a reload, a market
switch, a replay opened or closed — and never otherwise.

The readback for `feed.reconnect` and `feed.reload`: `connection_state`
says whether the feed is healthy, not whether a call respawned it,
and a reload normally lands on a connected feed. A client that lost
the answer compares this with its reading from before the call.
`#[serde(default)]` for the same reason as `history_reach_running`:
an optional field is an additive change to the v1 payload.

history_load.description:
This tab's history run: idle, queued behind the opening fill, loading
toward its target with how far back it has got, or paused while the
tab is off screen. Optional so a v1 payload recorded before it keeps
parsing; the application always reports it.

history_reach_note.description:
What the last *load older* press had to say, while it is still on
screen — the exact sentence the trader reads in the loading lane.

`null` is the ordinary state: no press yet, a press that landed what it
promised, or one whose remark has had its time. Here because the
outcome of a reach is the whole point of making one, and an operator
driving the button through `QUANTICK_LOAD_OLDER` or `quantick_invoke`
must be able to learn it from the same words rather than by diffing
bar counts.

history_reach_running.description:
Whether a run of *load older* requests is in flight right now.

`#[serde(default)]` keeps it out of the schema's `required` list, which
is what makes adding it here a *compatible* change to a v1 payload: the
control-plane contract (§5.6 of the development plan) counts a new
required field as breaking, and a v1 payload recorded by an earlier
build must keep deserializing. Absent reads as "no run", which is what
a build with no reach campaigns was in fact reporting.

latest_arrival_latency_ms.description: Signed local receipt stamp minus venue stamp; includes clock disagreement.

opening_slices_remaining.description:
Slices of the opening session still to arrive, while a source is
filling the chart in behind what it first painted.

Absent when nothing is filling, which is the steady state — so an
operator can tell "this chart is still arriving" from "this is all
there is", which `history_trade_count` alone cannot say: it rises with
no denominator.

stall.description:
The application's own judgement that this feed has stopped delivering,
or absent while it is merely slow.

Distinct from `notice`, which is what the *provider* said. A transport
that reports itself connected while nothing comes down it produces no
notice at all, and this is the only field that reports it — which is
exactly the case a client watching for a frozen terminal has to see.

tape_backfill.description:
The feed's refill of the hole its last reconnect left, while one runs
and after it ends. Absent on a tab whose feed never refilled one,
which is every feed but MetaTrader and every tab that never
reconnected; optional, so additive to v1.

tape_gaps.description:
Market-time bounds of source loss or a reconnect interruption.
Equal bounds can bracket known missing messages. Bounded, oldest first.

Omitted when there are none, so a reader written against the scope
before this field existed keeps parsing every payload from a tab that
never reconnected — which is nearly all of them.

HistoryBoundarySnapshot.description: Where a feed's pageable trade history ends.

oneOf.description: The venue retains no executions older than the chart holds.

HistoryLoadSnapshot.description: One tab's history run, as the History button draws it.

back_to_unix_ms.description: The oldest print held or fetched so far by the run.

main_reach.description: What the tab's main click loads.

reach.description: The target being loaded or queued; absent while idle.

sessions_reached.description: Previous sessions whose open the run has proven on the chart.

traded_ms.description: Traded time the run has counted.

from_open.description: Whether the recording started with the counter barely begun.

session_deals.description: The counter's last reading that day.

sources.description: Configured source pairs available to feed.source.set and the selectors.

snapshot_scopes.title: Feed status

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports frame timing, active work, indicator failures, and the last published order-flow health.

FeedIntegritySnapshot.description: Counts source messages, never estimates how many executed trades were lost.

IntakeLagSnapshot.description:
How long live prints waited inside one window drain before paper trading
saw them: the drain's receipt stamp (taken at its first live print) to the
paper-trading stage, per print, over a bounded window of the newest prints
(nearest-rank). Time spent queued before the drain began is not included;
`arrival_latency_ms` carries that. Wall-clock milliseconds: sub-millisecond
handling reads zero, and a forward clock step reads as lag.

clamped.description:
Of the prints the window covers, those whose stage stamp preceded the
receipt stamp (a wall-clock step back), counted as zero lag rather than
dropped.

floored_quantity.description: Exact quantity the trader's own display floor kept off the canvas.

folded_aggressions.description:
Aggressions the projection budget folded into a neighbour instead of
drawing alone. Folded, not dropped: the quantity is still on the canvas.

feed_integrity.description: Cumulative source diagnostics, independent of latency and gap eviction.

tape.description:
How late this tab's tape is, and where the time is going. `None` while
replaying — a recording's prints are as old as the day they were
captured and the playback clock decides when they appear.

trade_gate.description: Why new entries are paused on this tab; `null` while they are not.

TapeHealthSnapshot.description:
Where a tab's tape delay is being spent.

The whole point of the breakdown is that "the chart is eighteen seconds
behind" is not actionable on its own: it reads the same whether the venue's
adapter was late, the wire was late, or this process drained late, and those
have different fixes. An investigation that starts here can name the hop
without a screenshot and without a person watching the corner of a window.

arrival_latency_ms.description:
Signed local receipt stamp minus venue stamp, including clock disagreement.
Without a provider breakdown this is not transport latency. Local worker
residence and processing are measured separately on a monotonic clock.

dominant_hop.description: The provider's own name for the hop that owns most of the delay.

feed_arrival_latency_ms.description:
Provider receipt stamp minus venue stamp, one hop before chart drain.
Different clock domains may produce signed offsets; separately sampled
chart/provider values do not establish precise local queue residence.

intake_lag.description:
Drain-receipt-to-paper-trading delay over the newest live prints;
`None` before the feed session's first live print.

sampled_prints.description: How many live prints the split covers.

source_latency_ms.description:
Venue stamp to the source handing the print over: everything upstream
of quantick.

source_latency_peak_ms.description:
The worst `source_latency_ms` over the sampled prints.

The only peak reported, and deliberately: it is two source-side stamps
subtracted per print, so every print contributes with no clock involved.
A peak on the arrival or wire figures would need the reader's clock
applied to a print that arrived earlier, which measures that print's age
rather than its delay — on a quiet tape, the sampling interval itself.

transport_latency_ms.description: The source handing it over to quantick reading it: the wire.

TradeGateSnapshot.description:
New entries are paused because the chart is out of sync with its feed;
exits still work. Every reading is the one the pause was judged on.

latency_hop.description: The provider's name for the hop that owns most of it.

latency_ms.description: The provider's measured arrival latency; `null` without a split.

link.description: The chart's link to the feed: `up`, `attempting` or `offline`.

notice.description: What the feed's own notice says, when it says anything.

sentence.description: The refusal an entry answers with, as the toast says it.

tape_age_ms.description: Wall clock minus the newest event on the tape.

saves_off_unread_hooks.description:
Present when this session writes no store (decision DS7): the
`QUANTICK_*` names set at launch that this build does not read.

snapshot_scopes.title: Health summary

snapshot_scopes.description: Resolves the last painted pointer position to pane, axis, bar, flow cell, and drawing meaning.

AvailabilitySnapshot.description:
Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

carried.description:
The live book carried past its last confirmation to the lane's live
edge: the book as last confirmed, not depth observed there. Omitted
when false, so v1 readers remain compatible.

current_book_preview.description: Current book snapshot in chart forward space; no historical time claim.

held_tape_end_unix_ms.description:
Where the tape is held when the cell is the recorded book beside a
tape panned into the past; absent for every other cell. Optional on
the wire so v1 readers remain compatible with snapshots produced
before a tape could be held.

live_lane.description: The cell is today's book in the live lane; false on a held tape.

source_book_unix_ms.description:
Book timeline timestamp, preserved with cached frames: source event time
for updates, effective coverage start for snapshots (not local arrival).

source_book_update_id.description: Update ID of the exact current book used to build this painted frame.

start_slot.description:
The closed-bar slots under the cell. A cell that lies wholly in the
live lane or on a held tape has none: both bounds then equal the lane
boundary, and `live_lane` or `held_tape_end_unix_ms` says where it is.

time_averaged.description: Quantity is a duration-weighted mean, rather than instantaneous depth.

PointerSnapshot.description:
`screen_x_px` and `screen_y_px` keep their names for the clients already
reading them, but the unit is the window's **logical points** — what the
window lays out in, and what `scene.controls` reports a control's rectangle
in, so a pointer and a rectangle can be compared without a scale factor
neither side knows. On a 200% display the framebuffer holds twice these
numbers.

snapshot_scopes.title: Semantic cursor

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports the selected drawing and paper-trade row, with unsupported selections stated explicitly.

AnnotationBand.description:
Which value axis of the pane an annotation's anchor prices are read on.
Omitted: the candles' price axis, so every call written before indicator
bands existed means what it always meant.

oneOf.description: The candles' price axis.

One indicator pane's own value axis, named by the `kind` and `ordinal`
the pane's indicators snapshot reports (`native.cvd`, `0`). Anchor
`price` is then that indicator's value: a CVD level, not a price.

AvailabilitySnapshot.description:
Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

annotation_band.description:
The same band in the shape an `annotate.*.create` call takes as
`band`, so a listed mark's band can be handed straight back; absent for
a time-only mark, which has no value axis. Optional in the schema only
so v1 readers stay compatible.

snapshot_scopes.title: Current selection

snapshot_scopes.description: Bounded registered layer discovery and requested/effective visibility per stable pane ID; grid belongs to each pane.

effective.description: Visibility eligible under current layer policy; no pixel geometry is claimed.

persistence.description:
Where the switch is kept: `chart_layers`, the chart-layers file every
market shares; `orderflow_preset`, the bubble settings of the asset
the pane shows — saved only while that asset's save switch is on
(`orderflow.bubbles` reports it as `asset.save_changes`).

snapshot_scopes.title: Layer visibility

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports whether aggression bubbles are drawn over the chart and the lane, whether they are drawn as Bookmap-style volume dots, and what the display floor keeps off the canvas.

AvailabilitySnapshot.description:
Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

BubbleAssetSnapshot.description: The asset a pane's bubble settings belong to.

key.description:
The asset's key: the feed config's `symbol_bubble_presets` key that
names the symbol (`WIN*` covers every mini index contract), or the
symbol itself.

preset.description:
The preset the look on screen started from; empty once the panel's
defaults replaced it.

save_changes.description:
The asset's "Save changes for this asset" (default on), the same in
every tab on it; `orderflow.bubbles.save_changes.set` switches it.
Off, a change stays on the pane it was made on for this session — not
stored, not shown in other tabs on the asset, which show the stored
settings — and `saved` is `false` while one is on screen. Switched on
again, the switching pane's settings are stored for the asset, unless
its stored settings changed since that pane last showed them: then
the pane wears those instead (the action's result `screen` says
which).

save_error.description: Why they are not saved; absent when they are.

saved.description:
Whether the store file holds the settings this pane shows. `false`
until the next frame writes a change, while the file cannot be read
or written — they are kept in memory, retried, for this run only —
and while saving is off and a change is on screen.

source.description:
Where the settings came from: `stored` (changed for this asset; see
`saved`), `declared` (the preset the feed config declares) or
`default` (the presets file's active look).

aggression_provenance.description: Where the aggression these bubbles draw comes from.

asset.description:
The asset these bubble settings belong to. Every change made while
it is on screen — the panel, `layers.visibility.set` on `bubbles`,
`bubble_overlap_merge`, `native_tape`, `tape_only` and the flow
pane's `candle_aggression`, `orderflow.tape.opening_scale.set`, and
`orderflow.bubbles.size.set` —
belongs to this asset alone. While its `save_changes` is on it is
saved, reaches every tab showing the asset and is restored whenever
a tab shows it again; off, it stays on the pane it was made on for
the session. Wheeling or dragging the tape's window or width moves
the view only. Absent until the tab binds an asset.

depth_time_averaging.description:
Dense historical tape depth uses labelled duration-weighted averages;
current constant intervals remain exact.

display_scale.description: Independent final-radius gains; 1 preserves the selected preset's sizes.

floored_quantity.description:
The exact quantity the trader's own display floor keeps off the canvas.
Floored, not dropped: it is still in the totals.

fold_market_closed.description:
The tape goes away by itself while the market is closed: the asset's
setting, set by `orderflow.tape.market_fold.set`. It never writes `tape_view`.

forward_book_preview.description:
The strip between the last candle and the tape previews the current
book, read exactly while it is current. The lane setting
`forward_book_preview`, one of the asset's bubble settings.

ignore_opening_burst_in_scale.description:
Exclude the first recorded 100 ms burst from automatic tape-only
sizing; its factual volume is retained and its drawn radius capped.

lane_enabled.description: And over the live lane, which is a separate switch.

native_tape.description:
The tape is the native tape: each print at its own execution time
and price, on the market clock over the whole window, with one price
axis fitted by its prints (manual Y allowed). Beside the tick candles
it keeps its share of the pane behind a draggable divider, and moving
or zooming the candles never changes it. The tape the pane builds, not
the switch: true whenever `tape_only` is, and beside the candles only
with the tape on and `overlap_merge` (volume dots) on. The request is
the lane setting `native_tape`, one of the asset's bubble settings
(see `asset`), read back by `layers.visibility` as layer `native_tape`.

overlap_merge.description:
Bubbles use volume dots with a buy/sell pie. The ordinary chart and
lane use dots keyed by bars or market-time windows and price levels.
On the native tape, dots use quantity-weighted trade time and price;
the forming dot rides the right edge. Nearby recent prints may merge;
once they leave the live aggregation region, their membership stays
fixed while time and price axes transform their coordinates. The
default area scale follows the largest visible dot, drawn at the full
radius; neighbours may overlap. Grouping changes start a
new grouping; final-radius gains preserve it. The bubble setting `overlap_merge` is
switched by `layers.visibility.set` as layer `bubble_overlap_merge`.

preset.description: Whole-look selection, including unbound views; empty after defaults.

recorded_opening_windows_ms.description:
First recorded native window of each retained UTC day. For daytime
WIN sessions, this identifies the first available burst, not a proven
exchange auction. Empty until executions have been observed.

stable_size.description:
Native dots retain their factual groups. An optional viewport scale
changes their common presentation reference and radius after grouping.

tape_display_full_quantity.description:
The quantity drawn at the configured maximum radius for stable native
Tape with a fixed display reference. Its minimum radius remains visible;
area above that minimum grows with quantity up to this amount. Separate
from `volume_dots.volume_dot_full_quantity`, which still governs grouping.
Absent for automatic sizing and legacy native Tape looks.

tape_fold.description:
Which side the pane's view closes to a rail: `open`, `candles` (tape only)
or `tape` (the candles alone). A reading of `tape_view`, the one state:
dragging the divider to an edge and `orderflow.tape.fold.set` write that.

tape_fold_held_by_market.description:
The market holds the tape away right now. Runtime only; the first print,
the setting, a hand on the rail or a view change releases it.

tape_only.description:
The pane shows the tape alone, Bookmap style: the native tape takes
the whole canvas, no candle or candle mark is drawn and time runs
across the full width on the tape's own window. The lane setting
`tape_only`, switched by `layers.visibility.set` as layer `tape_only`.

tape_view.description:
Which view the tape's two switches ask for: `beside`, `candles` (alone)
or `tape` (alone). Set by the pane header's Trail and Tape switches,
Ctrl+Shift+R, Ctrl+Shift+T or `orderflow.tape.view.set`, and by dragging the
divider to an edge.

tape_viewport_scale.description: Visible-relative native Tape presentation, independent of grouping.

tick_presets.description: Chart-only presets available for this asset.

volume_dots.description:
The rungs and size scales the last volume-dots frame was built on;
absent when the pane last drew no dots.

FlowExecutionDisplayPolicy.description:
Emphasis changes neither source membership nor volume-proportional area.
Symbols may be separated above their source; reported prices remain factual.

oneOf.description: Legacy readback policy, retained for previously captured snapshots.

Ordinary regions remain dim through one quarter of the reference, then
brighten gradually up to the reference. Display separation never promotes
a small region. Oversized opening regions keep their faint treatment.

Peak spheres: every mass is drawn, its radius by rank among the
visible masses (`scale_basis` `ranked_visible_masses`), labels on the
top fifth; no mass is held back as dim context.

buy_radius_px.description: Radius of a disc with the same area as the buy sector; not a separate painted disc.

opening_capped.description: Legacy compatibility field, always false; radius_px reports actual area.

radius_px.description:
Actual painted circle radius: gross quantity determines its area, or
under `ranked_peak_masses` its rank among the visible masses does.

sell_radius_px.description: Radius of a disc with the same area as the sell sector; not a separate painted disc.

ordinal.description: Zero-based index in this pane's retained source at source_revision.

oneOf.description:
Peak spheres: radius by rank among the visible masses; the frame's
notes name how many and from which quantity labels are drawn.

large_region_threshold.description:
Inclusive placement threshold for ordinary regions. Above this volume,
brightness rises gradually to the effective reference; area is unchanged.

notes.description:
What this frame leaves out or infers (volume updating or partial,
excluded records, first-daily-region scaling). The chart paints no
caption for them; this is where they are read.

offscreen_executions.description: Loaded native cells outside the actual horizontal viewport, not missing source.

radius_limit_px.description: Ordinary reference radius; the first daily region can exceed it when excluded.

region_candles.description:
Whole candles a zoom region spans, chosen by the zoom; when present it
bounds a merge instead of `region_window_ms`.

region_window_ms.description: Intrinsic aligned interval before spatial pooling; never an order identifier.

ineligible_executions.description: Loaded source records excluded for nonpositive quantity or invalid tick denominator.

flow_execution.description: Retained executions aggregated into visible FLOW regions, separate from native Tape.

opening_scale.description: Independent reversible preferences, readable even when marks are hidden.

TapeFold.description: Which side of the pane is closed to a rail.

oneOf.description: Candles and tape side by side: the view `beside`.
The candles closed to a rail on the left: the view `tape`, tape only.
The tape closed to a rail on the right: the view `candles`, the tape off.

TapeView.description: What the flow pane shows: names the side shown.

oneOf.description: Candles and tape side by side at the tape's width share.
The candles alone; the tape is switched off.
The tape alone; no candle is drawn.

peak_spheres.description:
Each zoom region is divided at the peaks of its volume-by-price
profile: one sphere per peak, sized by rank among the spheres in view.

reference_quantity.description: Full-radius quantity in fixed mode; configured floor in visible-max mode.

viewport_scale.description: Present when final visible quantities and the current camera size the spheres.

zoom_regions.description:
Spheres merge inside whole candles chosen by the zoom, not one second
of market time; the frame's `region_candles` says how many. True
whenever `peak_spheres` is, which divides those same regions.

ViewportBubbleScaleSnapshot.description: Optional drawing calibration; factual grouping uses its existing settings.

x_units_per_pixel.description: Bars on candles; milliseconds on native Tape.

VolumeDotsSnapshot.description: What a volume-dots frame was keyed and sized on.

auto_full.description:
Each pane sizes its dots relative to its own biggest dot on screen
instead of `volume_dot_full_quantity`. The bubble setting
`volume_dot_auto_full`.

candle_level_ticks.description:
Native ticks per candle level, chosen from the candle price axis. A
candle dot is its whole bar at one level.

tape_level_ticks.description:
Native ticks per tape level, chosen from the price span of the tape's
own prints.

volume_dot_full_quantity.description:
The typed volume-dot reference (`volume_dot_full_quantity`). Native
Tape uses it to group recent prints; stable native Tape with a fixed
display reference draws against `tape_display_full_quantity` instead.
Other volume dots draw at the largest radius at this amount.

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports whether the candle footprint layer is drawn and the setup it is drawn with.

compact_from_px.description:
The configured candle width at which one summary number per row
starts, in both zoom directions, measured at a detail scale of 1.
Never above `detailed_from_px`: the effective entry the chart uses,
ordered under Detailed while the stored setting keeps its own value.

detail_scale.description:
The detail scale both widths are stretched by: a level starts near its
`*_from_px` times this, in candle pixels on screen. The product is
capped at the deepest zoom, and a style's own text floor can raise
it, so it is a configured entry, not a measured one.

detailed_from_px.description:
Candle width at which the ladder's full detail starts, in both zoom
directions; styles with more columns keep their ratio to it.

imbalance_minimum_quantity.description:
Quantity a level must reach before the ratio is applied at all, so a
one-lot against nothing is not called an imbalance.

imbalance_ratio.description:
A level is imbalanced when one side exceeds the diagonal other side by
this factor.

number_row_px.description:
The shortest a row with numbers may draw before neighbouring prices
merge ("min number row height"); the one-number level keeps a pixel
under it.

profile_row_px.description:
The shortest a profile band may draw before neighbouring prices merge
into one band ("min band height").

stacked_count.description: Consecutive imbalanced levels that make a stacked zone.

style.description:
`split`, `ladder`, `bid_ask`, `cluster` or `auto` — how each ladder is
read. `auto` is not a look of its own: it picks the richest reading the
zoom can pay for, again on every frame.

overridden.description:
True when this chart carries its own footprint setup rather than the
window's shared one.

visible.description: The candle footprint layer is drawn on this chart.

AvailabilitySnapshot.description:
Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

BookGapSnapshot.description:
Why the book is missing over some stretches of the chart: one row per reason,
sorted by it. The marks on the chart carry no words, so these and their hover
are what says so.

label.description: The same reason in the words the mark's hover shows.

reason.description: The stable reason history recorded, such as `sequence_gap`.

stretches.description: How many stretches of the last published frame carry it.

book_held_at_unix_ms.description:
Where the heat stops, in venue time, while the book goes on arriving: the
tape's window is held short of the clock because no print is coming, and
the book behind this instant is not drawn. Absent otherwise. The status
can read a live book beside it; both are true.

capture_price_grouping.description:
The bucket the engine is capturing at. The auto-base logic can move it
with no user action, so it is mirrored rather than assumed.

display_grouping.description:
How the captured buckets are merged for display: `native`,
`multiple_<n>` for a fixed multiple of the capture bucket, or
`adaptive_<rows>` — the default — which picks a multiple near that row
count for the visible price window.

gaps.description: Why the book is missing where the last frame marks a gap, if anywhere.

lane_visible.description: And over the live lane, which is a separate switch.

retention_ms.description: How long a resting level stays on the canvas after it leaves the book.

visible.description: Depth heat is drawn over the chart.

when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is

best_bid.description:
Best bid and ask of the *whole* book, even when they sit outside the
window the ladders below were clipped to.

price_grouping.description: The bucket the levels were captured at.

spread.description: Distance between the two best prices, when both exist.

status.description:
`disabled`, `connecting`, `buffering`, `syncing`, `live`, `error` — the
capture state, as a code rather than the badge's prose.

TabSettingsSnapshot.description: One tab's panel and its asset's folds, whether or not anything painted them.

asset.description: The asset whose sections these are.

lights_on.description:
The flow pane paints lit now: the lights are saved on and the theme
authors a lit surface (Light).

lights_saved.description: The lights as saved with the tab, whatever the theme paints.

schema.description: Every tab's panel, as it would save.

Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

LaneWindowSnapshot.description:
How wide the live lane's window is, said the way the setting says it. An
`auto` window follows the recent bars' typical duration, so publishing one
resolved number would report a measurement as a setting.

fixed_ms.description: Present for `fixed`: the exchange milliseconds shown in the band.

zoom.description: Present for `auto`: `1.0` fits about one bar's worth of market time.

age_ms.description:
How far behind the newest print the tape was running at the instant
this capture was taken. Absent while replaying — a recording is played
on its own clock and is never late — and before anything has arrived.

aggression_provenance.description: Where the aggressor side comes from on this tape.

last_event_unix_ms.description: Venue time of the newest print the order-flow engine has seen.

live_end_unix_ms.description:
The right edge of the live lane, in venue time. Absent when no flow
layer is drawn: a chart with no lane has no edge, and the newest print
the engine happens to have seen is not one.

live_lane_enabled.description: The live lane is drawn, and how its window is chosen.
