snapshot_scopes.description: Every control on screen with a frame-stable ID, its owner, whether it is selected, and the coded reason when it cannot be operated.

oneOf.description: The Home page: no chart is painted and no pane is listed.
The chart of the active market tab.

AvailabilitySnapshot.description:
Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

SceneBoundsSnapshot.description:
A control's rectangle in window coordinates, in **logical points**.

Not device pixels: the window lays out in points, and the two differ by the
display's scale factor — a canvas on a 200% display occupies twice these
numbers in the framebuffer. Reported as points anyway, because that is the
unit the pointer is reported in too (`interaction.cursor`), so the two
scopes can be compared without a conversion neither of them knows the
factor for. A client composing these with a screenshot must scale them
itself.

SceneControlSnapshot.description: One control the trader can see.

availability.description:
Whether operating it now would do anything, and the reason when not.

The reason is a stable code, never the sentence the interface shows.
A client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating it would break every such client at once.

bounds.description: Where the control is, when the frame already knows.

bounds_availability.description:
Why there are no bounds, when there are none.

Only the chart canvases record their rectangle during the frame they
are drawn. Measuring the chrome would mean writing a rectangle per
control per frame whether or not anyone is watching, which this module
refuses to do — so the answer is an honest "not recorded" rather than
a guess assembled from layout constants.

capability_id.description:
The registered capability that *operates* this control, where one
exists.

Absent on every control today, and honestly so: reading the screen came
before acting on it, and the cockpit tier that registers a capability
per control is still ahead. An absent ID means "not reachable through
the control plane yet", never "not reachable at all" — and a capability
that merely *reads about* a control (a page of a canvas's bars) is not
one that operates it, so it does not go here.

control_id.description:
Stable for as long as the control is what it is.

Derived from identity — a tab's ID, a pane's ID, a layer's or a tool's
declared name — never from a position on screen or an index into this
list. Two captures a hundred frames apart name the same button the same
way, which is what makes it possible to point at one, look away, and
point at it again.

description.description:
What the control shows or does, in the very words its tooltip carries,
where it has more to say than its label.

label.description: What the control is called, for a human reading the answer.

selected.description:
Whether the control is currently the chosen one of its group: the
active tab, the armed tool, the open dock tab, a layer that is drawn.

oneOf.description: The strip of open chart tabs.
The context toolbar above the canvas.
The drawing tool rail.
The right-hand dock.
One open chart tab, owning its panes.

The feed's offline corner, bottom-right of the chart.

Present only while the chart is not being fed — which is the whole
point of it, and why a capture with no `feed_status` control in it is
an operator's evidence that the feed is healthy rather than a gap in
the walk.

SceneOwnerSnapshot.description: Which region of the window a control belongs to.

id.description:
The owner's own identifier. Where the owner is itself a control in this
list — a chart tab owning its panes — this is that control's ID, so the
tree can be walked without a second vocabulary.

SceneRoleDto.description:
What kind of thing a control is, so a client can decide how to talk about
it without matching on its identifier.

oneOf.description: One of a strip of tabs; selecting it replaces what is below.
An on/off switch that stays where it is.
A mode the pointer enters until another is chosen.
A chart surface: the thing the pointer resolves against.

A control that does one thing and returns, leaving no mode behind.

The first role whose controls carry a `capability_id`: pressing one is
exactly a call, so the scene can say which call it is instead of
leaving an operator to guess from the label.

schema.description:
What is on screen right now, as controls an operator can name.

The tree is expressed as a flat list plus [`SceneControlSnapshot::owner`]
rather than as nested arrays: a client that wants the tree walks the owner
links, and a client that wants one control by ID does not have to descend
into anything to find it.

active_tab_id.description:
The market tab the window holds as active. While Home is the
[`Self::active_surface`] this market keeps running behind it.

coverage.description:
Whether `controls` is every control on screen. It never is yet.

Two things cut it, and this says which. Each covered region is walked
only as far as one group of it — a pane header's controls, the rail's
tools, the dock's tab strip, a tab's canvases — so a capture that has
truncated nothing is still not the screen, and reports as much rather
than letting a client read a short list as a complete one. Beyond
that the scene is bounded like every other projection, and a capture
that met the bound says so instead of truncating in silence.

covered_regions.description:
The regions this capture enumerated, in the order it walked them.

The honest bound on everything above: a control belonging to a region
absent from this list was not looked for, and its absence from
`controls` says nothing about whether it is on screen.

focused_pane_id.description:
The focused canvas, when this capture lists one.

Absent while the active tab is between layouts and has no painted
pane at all — an honest gap rather than an ID pointing at a control
`controls` does not contain.

window_id.description:
Live native market window, pinned once when this read reaches the UI thread.
Omission selects the focused live window at that admission point.

schema.title: SceneSnapshot

snapshot_scopes.title: Visible controls

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports the simulated position, the working orders and the closed-trade ledger, with its provenance declared.

entry_aggregate_id.description:
Aggregate ids of the prints that opened and closed the position — the
audit trail back to the tape. Absent only on rows loaded from a
version-1 history file, which did not record them.

fees_points.description:
Commission both sides of the round trip paid, never negative; zero
on a free fill model and on rows journaled before fees existed.
Optional in v1 only because servers before the fee model omit it.

maximum_adverse_excursion_points.description:
Worst excursion against the average entry while the position was open,
in points and never negative. Absent for version-1 rows: unknown is
not zero.

pnl_points.description: Points before fees; the account kept `pnl_points - fees_points`.

placed_unix_ms.description:
Venue time of the last print seen when the order was placed. The
simulator has no clock of its own.

price.description:
Limit price for a limit, trigger price for a stop, absent for a market
order — which has no price of its own by definition.

open_points.description:
Open profit in points — price units times quantity, signed. Points and
not currency: the workspace knows no per-instrument tick value, and a
number that cannot be computed honestly is not published. Absent
before any mark exists.

armed_strategy.description:
The named exit ladder the ticket is armed with, if any.

What the *next* order will carry, which the order rows below cannot
say: they are what already exists. An operator asked "why is nothing
projecting" has to be able to read this, and until it was here the
answer lived only in pixels.

armed_strategy_refusal.description:
Why the armed ladder cannot be used, when it cannot. Absent when it
is usable, and absent when nothing is armed — a strategy that draws
nothing and says nothing is the bug this field exists to prevent.

closed_trades_page_start.description:
Row of the whole ledger that `closed_trades[0]` stands for. Zero unless
the page was cut; published because the page is the ledger's *tail*, so
without it a row number here cannot be placed in the ledger the count
above describes.

closed_trades_truncated.description:
True when `closed_trades` was cut at its page limit. The newest rows
are kept: a ledger is read from its end.

provenance.description: Where these rows come from, named rather than implied.

risk_amount.description:
What that size stands to lose at the entry's own stop. Absent for the
same reasons as `risk_quantity`.

risk_blocks_entry.description: Whether the trader's lock is refusing this entry right now.

risk_currency.description:
The currency `risk_amount` is in. Nothing here converts between
currencies, so a reader comparing two tabs must compare these too.

risk_quantity.description:
The size the risk per trade derived, absent when it derived none —
the mode is off, or nothing here could be sized.

risk_sentence.description:
The sentence the ticket is showing, verbatim.

Produced by the same function that renders it on screen rather than a
second wording kept in step by hand: an operator reading this and a
trader reading the ticket are looking at one sentence. Absent only
when the mode is off and there is nothing to say.

risk_state.description:
What the risk per trade makes of the entry the ticket is holding:
`off`, `sized`, `short_of_budget`, `capped_at_max`,
`clamped_at_minimum`, `instrument_unknown`, `no_budget` or `refused`.

The state, not the pixels. An operator asked "why is the size 1" has
to be able to read the answer rather than infer it from a number.

ruler_ticks.description:
How far the aim's ruler stands from an entry, in ticks; zero when it
is not in use. Sticky across aims, so a reader needs it to explain
what the next order would carry.

selected_trade_row.description:
Row of the selected closed trade in the whole ledger — the same
numbering as `closed_trade_count`, not a position in the page above.
Subtract `closed_trades_page_start` to index `closed_trades`; a row
below that start was cut and is not on this page.

tick_size.description:
One tick of this tab's instrument, so `ruler_ticks` can be read as a
price rather than a count.

working_orders_truncated.description:
True when `working_orders` was cut at its page limit; the count above
still reports every order the simulator holds.

snapshot_scopes.title: Paper trading

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports which recording each tab is playing, where the playhead is, and whether a control trace sits beside it.

AvailabilitySnapshot.description:
Whether something is there to be read or acted on, and the coded reason
when it is not.

The reason is a stable identifier, never the sentence an interface shows a
human: a client made to parse that sentence would break the day it is
reworded, and translating the interface would break every such client at
once.

date.description:
Session day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, when the file name followed the
convention. Absent is honest: the recording did not say.

day_before.description:
The session day joined in front of this one, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when one was.

Two days on one chart is never left to be inferred from bar counts: an
operator asked to read the open needs to know whose order flow sits
behind it. Additive within v1.

day_before_prints.description:
How many prints in front of this session came from the day joined
before it — `0` when none was, and what turns the two counts above back
into the whole stream.

Additive within v1 (contract §4).

day_before_problem.description:
Why no day was joined, when there was a file for one and it could not
be used. `None` covers both "none was asked for" and "it joined".

The same reason the interface shows beside the transport, so the two
surfaces cannot disagree about why yesterday is missing. Additive.

elapsed_ms.description:
Wall time spent playing, which a seek resets — not the distance
travelled through the recording, which is `position_unix_ms`.

file_name.description:
The recording's file name only. The absolute path is deliberately not
published: it identifies nothing a client needs and would leak the
trader's directory layout to every observer.

played_trades.description:
Prints of *this session's own day* released so far, and how many it
holds — the two numbers the transport bar draws.

A day joined in front of the recording is context the chart was handed,
not part of the session being rehearsed, so it is counted out of both.
Publishing the raw cursor here instead would have an operator read
`played_trades = 1_504_020` beside `progress = 0` on a replay that has
not started, and disagree with the screen about the same session.

ReplayTraceSnapshot.description:
What the capture can honestly say about the control trace beside the
recording (contract §11): nothing, and where to ask instead.

Both halves were tried here and both are wrong on this thread. Reading the
sidecar to decide completeness is unbounded work. Even a bare existence
check is a `stat`, whose cost is the filesystem's and not this process's —
a recording on a network share or a cold path can take milliseconds, and a
capture of every scope already measures a p99 near
`CONTROL_UI_BUDGET_US`. So the capture does no file I/O at all and names
the gateway, which loads each recording's trace once and holds it.

file_name.description:
The name the sidecar would carry beside the recording, so a client can
ask the gateway about the right file without deriving the convention
itself.

state.description:
Whether a sidecar exists, and whether every recorded intent carries a
terminal result — the property that decides if the run is a
deterministic fixture. Both are served by the gateway; see the type
doc for why a capture answers neither.

replaying.description:
A tab playing no recording is live; `session` is then absent rather
than a zeroed row, so "not replaying" cannot be mistaken for "at the
start of a recording".

snapshot_scopes.title: Replay state

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports the Quantick build, target, protocol, and capture budget.
snapshot_scopes.title: System information

snapshot_scopes.description: Reports every tab and pane with stable IDs, visibility, and focus.

CanvasDimension.description: Which way a docked chart is resized.

oneOf.description: Along a split that lays charts left to right.
Along a split that lays charts top to bottom.

CanvasPaneDto.description: One pane of the canvas after the call.

height_share.description: The same along the nearest split laying them top to bottom.

railed.description:
A `minimized` chart a seam drag or a collapse call folded to a rail,
not to its menu strip; absent otherwise.

width_share.description:
A docked chart's share of the nearest split laying charts left to
right, to six places; absent when none holds it.

CanvasPlaceDto.description: A floating pane's place, rounded to whole points.

CanvasSeamDto.description:
One seam of the docked tree: what `canvas.seam.drag` takes as `path` and
`index`, which way it moves, and the rail beside it.

dimension.description:
What a drag of it trades: the widths of charts side by side, or the
heights of charts stacked.

index.description: It lies after child `index` of that split.

path.description:
The child indices from the root down to the split it divides; empty
for the root split.

rail_slot.description:
The first chart of the rail folded right beside it, which dragging
the seam back reopens; absent with no rail there.

resizable.description:
Whether a drag moves it: false beside menu strips up to the split's
end.

CanvasView.description:
One tab's canvas as the workspace summary reads it: the readback every
canvas edit reconciles against.

floating.description:
Where each floating pane stands, in whole points: over the canvas, or
on `monitor` for one in its own window.

preset_id.description: The preset the docked panes match; absent for a custom arrangement.

seams.description:
Every seam between docked panes, as `canvas.seam.drag` addresses it:
the root split's first, then each child split's, depth first. One
fewer than the docked panes at most; none while a chart is maximized.

LayoutTabSnapshot.description: One layout tab, as the strip lists it.

indicator_count.description: How many indicators the layout holds.

observed.description: None until this native viewport has supplied an observation.

source.description: Geometry is derived from the OS-fed native viewport, never from an accepted request.

PhysicalPlacement.description: Physical desktop pixels, including negative coordinates on secondary monitors.

WorkspaceColourDto.description:
A workspace's colour as the wire reads it: a preset names itself and its
index (`{"preset": "sky", "index": 2, ...}`), a custom colour its hex
(`{"custom": "#3A7BD5", ...}`); both give the value painted in each theme.
No two workspaces hold identical colours (`workspace.colour.set`).

custom.description: The custom colour's `#RRGGBB`; absent on a preset.

index.description: The preset's place in the palette, as files store it.

preset.description: The preset's name in lower case; absent on a custom colour.

collapsed.description: A folded pane retains its identity and data behind its rail.

layout_id.description: The layout this pane shows, by id in the strip.

pane_index.description: The pane's address within its tab — the number `layout.focus` takes.

canvas.description:
The canvas model: the preset the docked panes match and every pane's
mode. Additive; absent from a build that predates it.

context_collapsed.description:
Whether the context column is collapsed to its rail. A collapsed chart
is still counted `visible` in `panes`, because it comes back with its
bars and drawings; this is the one field that says it is put away.
The readback for `layout.pane.collapse` and `layout.pane.expand`, and
`#[serde(default)]` so it is an optional, additive field of the v1
payload.

flow_collapsed.description: The right-hand chart has a draggable rail instead of its body.

modified.description: Whether the tab holds edits it has not saved to that workspace.

venue.description: The tab's venue. Additive; empty from a build that predates it.

workspace.description:
The workspace this tab uses. Additive; empty from a build that predates
it.

workspace_colour.description:
That workspace's colour: the open tab's symbol and the capsule wear
it. Additive.

auto_save.description:
Whether layout edits are written into the tab's workspace as they are
made (`workspace.autosave.set`). Absent from an older answer: on.

history_reach.description:
How far one press of *load older* reaches, in the v1 vocabulary this
field has always used: `span` (an hours target; its length is
`history_reach_span_minutes`) or `previous-session` (yesterday). A
target that vocabulary has no word for — three or five days back —
reads as the empty string; `history_target` names every target.

Additive within v1 (contract §4): defaulted rather than required, so a
client holding this schema still validates a summary from an instance
built before the field existed.

history_reach_running.description:
Whether a run of *load older* requests is in flight on the active tab.

The setting above says what a press will do; this says whether one is
still doing it. Without it an operator that started a reach has no way
to tell a finished run from a running one except by polling bar counts
and guessing.

history_reach_span_minutes.description:
Minutes of *traded* time a press of the `span` reach pulls: the hours
target's own length while `history_reach` reads `span`, otherwise what
a legacy `span` token in a saved workspace or hook would load.

Beside the reach because the two are one choice: an operator that
can read back `by time` but not how much time cannot tell what the
next press will do.

`serde(default)` like every optional neighbour: v1 is frozen, and a
snapshot from a build that predates this field must still validate
against the shipped schema. A new *required* key is a breaking change
wearing an additive diff.

history_target.description:
What the History button's main click loads, as the token
`feed.history.load` takes: `hours:N` or `sessions:N`. Additive; empty
from a build that predates it.

layouts.description: The layout strip: every layout, and which is active. Additive.

progressive_venue_history.description:
Whether a feed that folds minutes builds its candle history a week
at a time. A feed serving every interval asks one page at the pane's
own interval either way, so the setting does not reach it.

replay_day_before.description:
Whether opening a recording joins the session day before it, and a
download fetches that day's tape as well.

Additive within v1 (contract §4). It decides what a replay an operator
is about to open will actually hold, so it has to be readable before
they open one — the bar counts afterwards are too late to plan with.

venue_lead_in.description:
Whether a chart cut by trades carries the venue's candles in front of
its bars. Read with each pane's `venue_prefix_present`: this is what
the trader asked for, that is what the pane actually holds.

windows.description: Native presentation order, independent of the retained runtime storage indices below.

workspaces.description:
Every workspace and its colour, `Default` first, then by name.
Additive; empty from a build that predates workspace colours.
